findings.finding: Buyer's color_read describes 'a raw, brushed-steel buckle (not painted or brightly colored plastic)' and contrasts it against 'the primary-colored plastic clips every cheap competitor uses.' Neither detail exists in brief.must_keep (which only specifies gauge, pull-test rating and stamped kg legend, nothing about finish) nor in scout.competitors' main_image_description fields (which describe plain 'plastic buckle' or 'plastic side-release buckle,' never a bright/primary color). The raw-unpainted-steel finish is exactly innovaty idea I6 ('Raw Matte Brushed-Steel Finish (No Paint, No Plating)'), which should not exist yet at buyer-phase. This is the classic buyer-saw-the-ideas contamination pattern.
findings.fix: Regenerate buyer.color_read from only brief + scout inputs (buyer should not know the finish decision yet), or, if the finish is meant to be a fixed brief constraint, move it explicitly into brief.seller_constraints.must_keep so the dependency is honest and traceable.

findings.finding: Genius states 'base-case contribution lands around 21% of price' in prose to the founder, but no contribution field appears anywhere in genius.json as an engine-computed output — contribution, break-even and the sanity rails are explicitly engine.py's job, not genius's. This looks like genius hand-calculated the figure (price minus referral, FBA, storage, ads, returns, landed cost) and is presenting it as if verified, which is exactly the 'no arithmetic by hand' rule this pipeline exists to prevent, and it is this same unverified number that justifies the 'stretch' feasibility verdict language to the founder.
findings.fix: Strip the specific '21%' claim from three_sentences_to_founder until engine.py has actually run the Monte Carlo/contribution calc on genius's ranges, then quote the engine's real output instead.

findings.finding: genius.versions[0].landed_cost_usd.base is $2.83, but recomputing from genius's own described buildup (BOM base sum $1.25 EXW + duty at stated ~14.5% of EXW ≈ $0.18 + freight at stated $180/cbm × stated 0.0009-0.0016 cbm/unit ≈ $0.15-0.29 + inbound-to-FBA stated $0.08-0.28) yields roughly $1.80-$2.20, not $2.83 — even pushing every sub-component to its stated high end only reaches about $2.22. There is a roughly $0.6-$1.0 unexplained gap between the narrative buildup and the headline number that feeds the 30%-of-price sanity rail and the recommended version's 'realistic' ruling for I1.
findings.fix: Publish the itemized dollar buildup for landed_cost_usd (EXW / freight / duty / inbound as separate dollar lines, not just a prose description) so the base figure is auditable, and reconcile the gap before it is used to justify I1's feasibility ruling.

findings.finding: The webbing and steel-buckle BOM lines say 'live web search (Sep 2026) found 25mm nylon webbing quoted $0.10-0.56/m' and 'live web search... found generic zinc-alloy/aluminum ladder-lock buckles at $0.01-0.82/unit.' These are the two largest EXW cost drivers, sourced by genius running its own search rather than citing a scout fact_id — a direct break of 'scout searches; everyone else cites scout's fact_ids,' with no confidence rating and no entry in scout.facts to check.
findings.fix: Route these two component-price lookups back to scout so they get a fact_id, source URL and confidence rating like every other market claim, or clearly re-label them as genius's own unverified placeholder (not 'live web search found') pending two real supplier quotes.

findings.finding: The main_image prompt depicts 'a small bright-orange tab... visible just inside the pawl housing peeking out' (idea I3's lock-engagement indicator), and the packaging prompt depicts 'a small matte-steel spare ladder-lock buckle nested in its own die-cut cardboard pocket' (the bundle_or_addition spare-buckle insert). Genius's recommended, funded launch scope is v1_hero_lean = I1 + I2 + I6 only — I3's overmold and the spare-buckle bundle are both absent from v1's BOM and explicitly deferred to v2/fast-follow. If v1 ships as recommended, the commissioned product/packaging photography will show a product the customer will not actually receive.
findings.fix: Regenerate the main_image and packaging image prompts scoped strictly to what v1_hero_lean actually ships (I1 buckle + I2 stitch + I6 raw finish; no orange tab, no spare-buckle-in-box), and only reintroduce those elements in a v2 photo refresh once I3/bundle_or_addition are actually funded.

findings.finding: I1's mechanism cites 'the sharp edge F6 identifies as the micro-abrasion point where 87% of buckle failures start' as settled fact. F6 is a single medium-confidence marketing/blog source (an Alibaba 'product insights' page) reporting an industry-article's own 'attributed to' hypothesis, not a controlled study. The C1 cluster this idea is built to fix (50% of negative sentiment, driving I1's hero status and the ~$4,500-$17,500 tooling+FTO spend) itself rests on only two travel-forum threads (F6, F7) plus one low-confidence anecdote (F8) — scout's own gaps section admits this was triangulated from forum anecdotes, not a direct read of real 1-2 star review pages.
findings.fix: Have scout mine actual 1-2 star review pages on 2-3 real competitor ASINs to corroborate (or correct) the 87%/50% figures before the tooling and FTO spend on I1 is locked in; treat the current numbers as directional in the interim.

findings.finding: buy_driver.pain_level is tagged 'extreme' (law.pain_extreme: 'price sensitivity collapses, speed and certainty win'), but buyer's own quantified outputs read as moderate pain: the price signal in three_second_scan is scored 'neutral' (not 'pull'), a real price ceiling exists (price_psychology.max_with_reason_usd: 22), and buy probability tops out at only 0.5 even once every top fear is answered by the bullets. That is 'searching and comparing, listing must finish the argument' (law.pain_moderate), not a buyer whose price sensitivity has collapsed. The inflated depth label likely pushes downstream pricing/share optimism higher than the buyer's own numbers support.
findings.fix: Either relabel pain_level as moderate and re-derive price_psychology/purchase_probability_current consistently, or if extreme is genuinely correct, raise the buy probability and drop the stated price ceiling to match a buyer for whom price has actually stopped mattering.

findings.finding: genius applies the required 25% stale-widening formula correctly, but because scout's own starting fba_fee_usd range was already narrow (±9.3% around base), the widened result (low $3.31 / base $3.75 / high $4.19) is still only ±11.7% around base — far short of the ±30% bar for an uncertain, not-independently-fetched dollar figure that directly sets the contribution-margin sanity rail.
findings.fix: Fetch the real per-unit FBA fee from a live Amazon FBA revenue calculator for this weight/size tier rather than carrying forward a mechanically-widened but still-narrow placeholder.

findings.finding: term_monthly_units (base 24,000/month) has zero grounding in any scout fact — scout.gaps explicitly states est_monthly_units 'was not obtainable from a tracker page for any competitor.' Genius's own assumption text admits it is 'genius's own order-of-magnitude estimate... informed by' a qualitative read of the competitive set, then applies the same ±40% width used elsewhere in the forecast as if it carried the same evidentiary weight as a sourced figure. This number is the base of the entire revenue/share/annual-unit chain.
findings.fix: Get even an indirect unit-volume proxy (review-count growth rate, BSR-based estimator, or a Helium10/Jungle Scout pull) for the top competitors before this figure is used to size ad spend, and mark it with materially wider bounds or lower confidence than sourced fee inputs until then.

findings.finding: The tariff-shift premortem item (probability 0.25, impact 'fatal') costs its mitigation at only $500-$1,200 for 'holding a backup Vietnam supplier quote in reserve' — that covers only the option, not the cost of actually executing an origin switch (new tooling amortization, re-qualification, requalifying packaging/dimensions) if the risk fires. A fatal-impact risk's mitigation cost should not read as this cheap.
findings.fix: Add a second cost line for actually activating the mitigation (re-tooling/re-qualifying a new origin), separate from the cheap cost of merely holding a quote.

findings.finding: The Amazon claims-suppression premortem item is costed at exactly $0 ('already fully captured... zero incremental spend'), the textbook 'mitigation that costs nothing' pattern this review is meant to catch. Even granting the lab-test line is shared with another budget item, a real claims-suppression event would still cost legal/compliance review time and a relisting delay that isn't reflected anywhere.
findings.fix: Add a small nominal legal/compliance review line instead of $0, and note the relisting-delay time cost even if the dollar cost stays low.

findings.finding: The claim 'painted/chrome/multi-color buckle and webbing finishes that add cost without addressing the buyer's actual fear... every page-one competitor spends on instead of load rating' cites F5 and F9, but F5 is about search-term/buckle-type dominance (plastic quick-release vs. steel ratchet) and F9 is about a plastic buckle's 30kg load rating — neither fact actually discusses paint, chrome or color finishes. This misattributed citation is the same root issue behind the unsupported 'stark white background' / 'primary-colored plastic clips' color-anchor claims (see K1).
findings.fix: Either find an actual source for the finish-spend claim or drop the F5/F9 citations and justify eliminating painted/chrome finishes on cost-and-simplicity grounds alone.

three_things_the_founder_must_hear: The '~21% contribution margin' and the landed-cost figure behind the 'stretch' verdict were both hand-built outside engine.py and the landed-cost math genius shows doesn't visibly add up to the $2.83 it reports — treat neither number as real until engine.py actually runs it.

The evidence under the hero buckle idea (the 50%-of-negatives C1 cluster and its '87% of failures' stat) comes from two forum threads and one blog article, not real review-mining, and the entire year-one revenue forecast is built on a 24,000-units/month market-size guess that scout admits it could never actually source — the money and the volume in this plan are both softer than the ranges make them look.

If you launch the recommended lean version (steel buckle + reinforced stitch + raw finish only, no orange lock-indicator tab, no spare-buckle bundle), fix the product and packaging photo briefs before paying for photography — as written today they show a lock-indicator tab and a spare buckle that this launch version does not actually include.
